messages:
Samir: Quick heads-up — we need a compact telemetry + routing contract for tier-aware routing and model-variant fallback. Goals: correct billing attribution, enforce isolation (no accidental dedicated->hosted leaks), and fast detection of spillover blackholes.

Maya: Agree. Minimal telemetry fields: tenant_id_hash:v2, tier, model, variant, route (enum), fallback_used (bool), fallback_reason, route_region, egress_node, sampling_rate.

Choi: For internal headers I'd add: `X-RW-Tier`, `X-RW-Model`, `X-RW-Variant`, `X-RW-Route`, `X-RW-Fallback` (`none`/`variant_hop`/`region_hop`/`hosted_spillover`), and `X-RW-Trace-Id`.

Choi: Router pseudo-code to illustrate priorities:
```
route = prefer_same_variant(local_pool)
if route.capacity_exhausted:
  route = prefer_cheaper_variant(local_pool)
if route.capacity_exhausted:
  route = region_swap_if_allowed(tenant)
if route.capacity_exhausted and tenant.allow_spillover:
  route = hosted_spillover()
else:
  return 429
```

Lia: Privacy rules: never emit raw tenant IDs. Use `tenant_id_hash:v2` with rotating salt stored in secrets manager. Include `sampled_request_id` only at low sample rates to pull payloads into secure debugging flows.

Kaela: Console metrics to expose: `routes.fallback_rate_by_tier`, `routes.p95_latency_by_route`, `routes.error_rate_by_route`, `routes.token_cost_delta_by_tenant_sample`. Alert baseline: fallback_rate > 0.5% for 10m on any dedicated tier.

infra-ops: infra-ops:router-config v0.7.3 canary started (10% nodes). Added acceptance tests for `X-RW-Tier` header.

Samir: Policy Q: Do we ever permit dedicated->hosted spillover for Enterprise/ISV contracts? Legal likely blocks by default.

Maya: Tenant flag: `allow_spillover` (true/false) on tenant profile. Default false for enterprise; default true for self-serve tiers. Router must check before any cross-environment routing.

Choi: For observability include `chosen_route` and an ordered `fallback_chain` field. If we need to limit payload size, emit `fallback_chain_hash` and record full chain in traces for sampled requests.

Lia: Add KV/prefix cache signals to telemetry: `kv_cache_hit_count` and `prefix_cache_hit` (bool) so we can diagnose cost/latency regressions caused by cache churn.

Kaela: UX idea: trace link in request panel should show route timeline (timestamps where each hop occurred), the cost delta (estimate), and the `fallback_chain`. Filter by `tenant_id_hash`/`tier`/`model`.

deploy-bot: canary v0.7.3 -> routers (10%). Monitoring: watch `routes.fallback_rate_by_tier`, `router.error_rate`, and `billing.attribution_mismatches`.

Samir: Action items: I'll draft an RFC (rfc/routing-telemetry-contract.md) with header defs, enums, console mockups, and a test plan. @Choi @Maya @Lia please review. Target: PR by EOW.

Maya: I'll write the synthetic test plan: simulate variant exhaustion and assert headers and telemetry are emitted within 30s, and that tenant `allow_spillover=false` results in 429s only.

Choi: I'll prototype the `route_reason` enum and header parsing in the router lib, and add unit tests for fallback_chain serialization.

Lia: I'll add the privacy appendix: salt rotation policy, retention windows for sampled payloads, and RBAC for full-request pull.

Kaela: I'll mock the dashboard tiles and draft an alert runbook for fallback spikes and for accidental hosted spillover.

Samir: Perfect. Ping this thread for blockers (infra quotas, legal flags, or RBAC changes). Thanks!
